solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drop insects in leisure wear

parts.note: to skip something is to drop or omit it

explanation.surface: Someone shaking bugs out of their casual trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: SKI PANTS are the trousers worn for skiing or lounging.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting stretch trousers, commonly worn as casual clothing.

clue.text: Singular old house in entertainment district

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
O is a standard abbreviation for old
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A curious ancient building standing among the theatres and clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is the London district famous for theatres, restaurants and nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho in London's West End is known for its bars, clubs and theatres, a classic nightlife quarter.

clue.text: Posing as priest, moaning pitifully

indicators.note: done pitifully means done badly, so the letters before it come out in a sorry jumble

explanation.surface: A fraudster pretending to be a cleric, whining in a pathetic way.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonating someone means pretending to be them, which is posing as them.

clue.text: A drink to have a day, up to the time of a party

parts.note: MON is the abbreviation for Monday
till means until, up to the time of

explanation.surface: Advice to enjoy one drink a day until the party comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: AMONTILLADO is a medium-dry Spanish sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a type of sherry, a fortified wine, so it is a drink.

clue.text: One working the land is calmer, not needing spades

indicators.note: not needing something means doing without it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A farmhand who is more relaxed without needing a shovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To till is to plough and cultivate soil, so a tiller is someone who farms.

clue.text: A little fantastic wine

indicators.note: a little of the next word means just a small part of it, sitting inside

parts.note: the middle stretch of this word

explanation.surface: A small amount of a superb wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sweet sparkling Italian wine named after its home town.

clue.text: Leaving out binders, give these a twirl?

parts.note: skipping something means leaving it out
ropes are used to bind things

explanation.surface: Omitting folders, then inviting someone to spin round.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic, signalled by the question mark: skipping ropes are swung round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is turned over the head and under the feet in a repeated circular motion.

clue.text: Tiny hero failed on paper

indicators.note: something that failed has gone wrong, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A small champion fell short in the written exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds as a plan or idea but may not work in practice, the same idiom.

clue.text: Very fashionable river for aquatic creature

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A trendy waterway that suits a creature of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus spends most of the day in rivers and lakes, so it is a water-loving animal.

clue.text: No Conservative went first

parts.note: 1ST is first, with the digit read as I

explanation.surface: A non-Tory politician who departed ahead of the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative is the British right-wing party, so a leftist is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftist holds socialist or progressive views, the opposite of a Conservative in politics.

clue.text: Changing frame futile in this full-length work

indicators.note: changing something alters its form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor saying that altering one shot would be pointless in a long movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A feature film is the main full-length cinema movie, as opposed to a short.

clue.text: Enter laptop for repair, one liable to spread infection

indicators.note: a thing in for repair is taken apart and rebuilt, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Handing in a computer to be fixed, as it might carry a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: The computer virus picture misleads: the definition is the proverbial bad apple that spoils the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten apple is a corrupt person whose bad influence spreads to others, like decay through a barrel.

clue.text: Fried noodles — dog chewed mine

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog

indicators.note: chewed means mangled by teeth, so the word after it is mashed up

explanation.surface: Complaining that the dog ate my takeaway noodles.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of stir-fried noodles with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Rings to be put in hard place, a fair game

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the first item goes between the letters that follow

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
rings look like the letter O, two of them
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: Hoops must be set up somewhere difficult for a fairground stall.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Os go inside H and PL, then A follows. Hoopla is a game where rings are thrown over prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground stall game in which players throw rings to land over prizes.

clue.text: Dasher, and part of his sleigh

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who dashes, a sprinter
second meaning: one of the long strips a sleigh slides on

explanation.surface: Dasher the reindeer and a piece of the sleigh he pulls.
explanation.walkthrough: Dasher looks like Santa's reindeer, but here it simply means one who dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is both a person who runs and a blade on which a sleigh glides over snow.

clue.text: Notice a means of escape coming

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a vent lets air or gas escape

explanation.surface: A warning that an escape route is on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, the coming of something important.

clue.text: Deterioration with muscle injury after sport

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
a torn muscle is a tear

explanation.surface: Physical decline from a pulled muscle picked up playing games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after sport' places the injury after WEAR; sport is the verb meaning to have on.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is the gradual damage things suffer from ordinary use, which is deterioration.

clue.text: Almost begin to take principal role

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

explanation.surface: An actor nearly beginning to play the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last T of START.
explanation.definitionFit: To star in a film or play is to have the leading part.

clue.text: Records poem, storing one instalment

indicators.note: storing something means keeping it inside, so one item sits within another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Discs and verse kept together as one part of a serial.
explanation.walkthrough: EP stands for extended play, a record longer than a single but shorter than an album.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment of a serialised story or television series.

clue.text: Data for entry is put in in the wrong order

indicators.note: wrong order says the words given must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Information to be keyed in has been entered jumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the two words is all the rearranging needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the information fed into a computer or system.

clue.text: Close — of day, almost

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: with Close read again, the close of day is night

explanation.surface: Nearly the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Close works twice: as the definition, and with 'of day' as the close of day, which is NIGHT, losing its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near, so it means close.

clue.text: Sprayer initially annoying to one who's near

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: near means stingy, so a near person is a skinflint

explanation.surface: An aerosol bothering a stingy neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like close by, but here it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid such as perfume into a fine spray.
